provenance.selection: Owner selected the ink and paper direction from the rendered directions. This slice applies its warm newsprint, Archivo display face, spot ink, panel offset, and masthead rule. The masthead keeps no utility controls: theme and sign out live on the Account page, the active nav rule spans exactly its item, and the team card puts the provider jump-out with the name. Royal violet and gold remain the approved identity; gold is reserved for the mark.

narrative.overview:
Lineupgrade reads as a printed sports sheet: warm newsprint, near-black ink, a display face for the page and the teams, and Schibsted for the work in between. Section rules are 3px ink; row hairlines stay 1px. Team cards and queue groups are the same plain 2px-ruled box on paper, set at least 24px apart. Royal violet is spent on interaction, gold exists only in the mark, and one spot ink marks urgency. The product is calm enough to check in the morning and precise enough to trust with a lineup.

This is an Operate product: information before spectacle, familiar controls, direct labels, and honest state. Light is warm newsprint; dark is a tinted violet sheet. Both are complete palettes.
keyCharacteristics: Archivo Variable for the display, page title, name title, section title, and card title types at 800; Schibsted Grotesk Variable for body, body strong, meta, label, and badge
Square everywhere; 3px ink section rules, 1px row hairlines, and a 2px ink rule around each team card
One 680px measure and one solid action per view
One 2px ink frame for every card, and no shadow beyond the focus ring
Decimals stay proportional; tabular figures only for integers compared in a column
Royal violet for interaction; gold only in the mark; spot ink only for urgency
Phones use one equal-width action row; a card badge keeps the top-right corner while a long name wraps

rules.name: The One Violet Rule
rules.body: Per view, one solid violet element: the primary action. Links and live controls carry violet as text, underline, or border. Everything else is ink, soft ink, and rule. Danger is a semantic exception.

rules.name: The Gold Reserve Rule
rules.body: Gold belongs to the mark and nowhere else. It is not a status, a highlight, a badge, or a second action.

rules.name: The Spot Ink Rule
rules.body: Spot ink is reserved for three urgency marks: a group that runs immediately, a roster that blocks adds and drops, and the printed stamp. It is not an error colour; danger owns errors and destructive actions.

rules.name: The Rule, Not a Box Rule
rules.body: A section title owns one 3px ink rule. Connection rows own 1px hairlines between them. Team cards and queue groups own the same 2px ink rule each. Status and empty states use a leading rule or plain text, never a dashed or bordered card.

rules.name: The Queue Panel Rule
rules.body: A queue group uses the shared card frame: 2px ink, paper ground, and at least 24px between cards. Team cards use the same frame. No surface casts a shadow.

rules.name: The Wordmark Rule
rules.body: The wordmark stays continuous lowercase lineupgrade in Schibsted Grotesk at the 11px label weight and tracking, beside the square mark. Archivo never sets the wordmark. Gold appears nowhere else.

rules.name: The Single Action Row Rule
rules.body: On phones every action in a bar shares one equal-width row, ordered destructive, tertiary, secondary, primary. A lone action fills the row. An action area holds at most three actions; more belong in an overflow menu. Labels never truncate: a label may wrap and every button in the row takes the tallest height.

rules.name: The Fixed Badge Rule
rules.body: A card header is a two-column grid. The title and meta take the remaining width, and the badge keeps the top-right corner at every size. A long name wraps inside its column and never pushes the badge below.

dos: Do use semantic tokens and both complete themes.
Do keep controls, inputs, badges, and dialogs square.
Do keep the 680px measure and let tables exceed it only with a reason.
Do use one 3px ink rule under a section title and 1px hairlines between list rows.
Do set display, page, name, section, and card titles in Archivo at weight 800.
Do choose a named text type and let it own its size, weight, line height, and tracking.
Do spend violet once per view on the primary action.
Do apply tabular numerals to comparable numbers only.
Do keep the wordmark lowercase in Schibsted and the mark gold.
Do frame every card with the same 2px ink rule and at least 24px between cards.
Do reserve spot ink for urgency.
Do preserve keyboard access, visible focus, selection, zoom, and reduced motion.
Do use short verb-led action labels and let a label wrap instead of cutting it off.
Do keep the card badge in the top-right corner and give the title the remaining width.
donts: Don't add border radii, a shadow beyond the focus ring, a colour gradient beyond the phone submit sheet fade, or a second accent.
Don't use gold outside the mark.
Don't use a serif or a third face.
Don't set body, body strong, meta, label, badge, or the wordmark in Archivo.
Don't pick a raw text size or weight at a call site.
Don't use spot ink for errors, destructive actions, or general status; danger owns those.
Don't box prose, connection rows, notices, or empty states.
Don't add letter spacing to body text or apply tabular figures to prose.
Don't repeat a control label on every row of a list.
Don't float controls to the right of a metadata line.
Don't use colour alone for connection, automation, or risk.
